goldens.comment: Consider adding try-catch around the await to handle import failures gracefully

The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/vital/lib/reschedule.ts:125 — Unawaited async forEach allows rescheduling to complete before calendar/video deletion begins; import or deletion failures are unobserved.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...})` is used with an async callback, but forEach does not await the promises returned by async callbacks. This means the function will continue execution without waiting for the calendar deletion operations to complete. Additionally, any errors thrown inside the async callback will be unhandled since forEach doesn't return promises. This is a real bug introduced by the change from synchronous to asynchronous getCalendar.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts:125 — Unawaited async forEach lets the reschedule flow finish before deferred calendar/video cleanup, with failures escaping surrounding control flow.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that in packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts, the forEach callback is changed to async (line 125: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {`), but forEach does not await async callbacks. This means the promises returned by `getCalendar()` and subsequent `deleteEvent()` or `deleteMeeting()` calls will not be awaited, causing the function to continue/complete before these operations finish. Any errors thrown in these async callbacks will not be caught by the surrounding try-catch block. This is a real bug that affects the correctness of the reschedule cleanup flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx:553 — Discarded async forEach callback means the booking reschedule endpoint does not await dynamically loaded calendar/video deletion work or surface its failures.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows at line 553 that `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {` is used with an async callback. The `forEach` method does not await the promises returned by async callbacks - it simply discards them. This means the calendar deletion operations (`calendar?.deleteEvent(...)`) and video meeting deletions will not be awaited, and any errors they throw will not be caught or surfaced. This is a real bug introduced by the change from synchronous to asynchronous `getCalendar`, as the code now has async operations inside forEach that won't be properly awaited.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/index.ts:2 — Imports run eagerly while constructing appStore, loading every integration instead of deferring unused app-store packages.

adjudication.rationale: The finding misreads the diff. The new code uses dynamic `import()` expressions (e.g., `applecalendar: import("./applecalendar")`) which return Promises and are NOT eagerly loaded at module construction time. Dynamic imports are deferred - they only start loading when the Promise is awaited. The diff shows the change FROM static imports (which were eager) TO dynamic imports (which are lazy/deferred). The finding claims the opposite of what the code actually does.
